customerJourneyStories.name: From carrier portals to one shipping platform
customerJourneyStories.summary: A growing webshop replaces several carrier portals and a basic shipping plugin with DeliveryMatch.

stages.narrative: After a peak season of manual label printing, missed cut-offs and complaints about wrong delivery dates, the operations manager is asked to make shipping scale without hiring.
She finds DeliveryMatch through its listing as best shipping software in the Emerce Top 100, its integration page for the webshop platform in use, and a peer retailer's case.

She compares DeliveryMatch with self-service shipping tools on carrier coverage, dynamic checkout, multi-warehouse support and price, requests a demo and checks references and the ISO 27001 certificate.
A fixed project manager connects the webshop and two carriers; one product category runs through DeliveryMatch for a few weeks while the rest stays on the old process.
All orders flow through rules and scan-to-ship; the team adds a third carrier, branded track-and-trace and the returns portal.
She stays because carrier changes no longer need IT work and checkout options keep converting; the next step is Carrier Invoice Control and the dynamic checkout for evening delivery.

customerJourneyStories.name: Adding a shipping control layer to the ERP
customerJourneyStories.summary: A wholesaler connects DeliveryMatch to its ERP after years of carrier portals and an outsourced parcel pickup.

stages.narrative: A growing share of direct and export orders makes carrier portals and manual CMRs untenable, and the finance team questions transport invoices.
The logistics manager hears of DeliveryMatch through the ERP implementation partner's integration list, a logistics trade fair (ICT & Logistiek) and the Nederlandse Logistiek Prijs 2025.
He checks that the ERP connector exists, that pallet carriers and ADR documents are supported, that Carrier Invoice Control is available, and reviews the ISO 27001 certificate with IT.
Parcels for one customer segment run through DeliveryMatch first; pallets follow once the freight carrier's labels are approved.
All outbound transport is booked from the ERP; customer agreements are rules and invoices are audited monthly.
He renews because transport cost per customer is finally visible and new export countries go live without projects.

customerJourneyStories.summary: A growing 3PL adds DeliveryMatch above its WMS to handle many clients and carriers.

stages.narrative: A new large client wants carriers the WMS's built-in shipping cannot handle, and every client onboarding now takes weeks of carrier setup.
The operations lead discovers DeliveryMatch through the WMS vendor's integration list and a joint stand with Monta WMS at ICT & Logistiek.
She checks the WMS connector, multi-client setup, sales rates per client and scan-to-ship speed in a demo, and compares with the WMS's native shipping and enterprise delivery-management suites.
One client and two pack stations run on DeliveryMatch for a month in parallel with the old process.
All clients are moved; new clients are onboarded as sub-accounts with their own carriers, branding and price lists.
She stays because onboarding time dropped and Carrier Invoice Control protects the shipping margin; she now refers clients to DeliveryMatch's dynamic checkout.

customerJourneyStories.name: Becoming a DeliveryMatch integration partner
customerJourneyStories.summary: A WMS vendor (or a Katapull sibling) embeds DeliveryMatch instead of building carrier links.

stages.narrative: The vendor loses deals because prospects need carriers and dynamic checkout the product does not support, and carrier maintenance eats development capacity.
The partner manager learns of the integration partner programme from joint customers, the Katapull group network and events such as the idyn webinar for Business Central partners.
They review API documentation, carrier coverage, commercial model and support responsibilities, and compare with nShift and Sendcloud partner programmes.
A first integration goes live with a few joint customers; webhooks and labels are tested in production.
The integration is listed on both sites; sales teams co-sell and refer customers.
The partnership lasts because shipping features keep growing without partner development, and inside Katapull the bridges become part of the Commerce Hub offer.

customerJourneyStories.name: Learning to trust a shop's delivery promise
customerJourneyStories.summary: A shopper meets DeliveryMatch only through a merchant's checkout, messages and returns portal.

stages.narrative: A missed delivery from another shop makes the shopper look for delivery certainty before buying.
She notices that this shop shows exact delivery dates and pickup points in the checkout, powered invisibly by DeliveryMatch.
She compares the shown date, cost and CO2 of options and decides whether to wait for a complete order or accept a split delivery.
The first order arrives on the chosen day; updates came from the shop by e-mail and WhatsApp.
She routinely picks the pickup point the checkout suggests and returns one item through the shop's portal.
She keeps buying because delivery and returns were predictable; the shop sees it as repeat purchases.
